newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Electrabel supply contracts.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Electrabel supply contracts.

text.p: The European Commission said in a statement on Friday it was happy with revised plans by Belgian elecricity company Electrabel to conclude long-term supply contracts with Belgium's municipally-owned distribution companies.

"At the initiative of Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, the Commission has suspended the action it had started against Electrabel and the (municipalities) concerning a possible breach of European competition law," the Commission said.
The Commission said the deal would eventually open the Belgian market to new independent power producers or other European producers, helping cut household and small company energy bills.
Under the deal, the distributors will be able to source up to 25 percent of their electricity needs from other suppliers after 2006.

"This should lead to an opening of around 1,000 MegaWatts, or the equivalent of five independent producers equipped, for example, with gas turbines of 200 MW or one nuclear power station of 900 MW," the Commission said.
In addition, from 2011, the distributors would be free to source the whole of their needs from other producers and break off their contracts with Electrabel (under agreed compensation terms).
Belgium's 17 municipally-owned distribution companies control more than 80 percent of its electricity market.
In 1996, Electrabel began concluding new exclusive, supply agreements with the distributors, sometimes lasting up to 30 years.
In return, the towns and municipalities that own the distributors were offered a share of five percent of Electrabel's capital in the form of shares.
The Commission concluded that these new agreements would have broken EU competition rules and ordered them to be changed.

The Commission said its statement on Friday did not represent a final ruling on the case. It would only formally clear the modified supply contracts once they had been drawn up and adopted by the distribution companies and Electrabel, a process which would take several months.
